rationale: Arbitrary-precision frontend literals retain their witness and IR node, then are range-checked before Verilog-2001 emission.
Opaque public-parameter identities survive capture and references resolve only in the declaring module scope.
Opaque local-parameter identities survive capture and resolve through an acyclic dependency graph before dependency-first emission.
Generate indices resolve only inside their owning generate body and remain symbolic in indexed part-select offsets.
Dual-valued addition retains the exact AST and interval analysis proves the complete legal result domain.
Dual-valued subtraction retains operand association and interval analysis proves the complete legal result domain.
All interval endpoint products bound the complete legal result domain while generate-index multiplication remains lexically scoped.
Dual-valued unary negation retains grouping and is range-checked before target lowering.
A stable frontend zero-witness guard plus whole-domain nonzero-divisor proof preserve explicit signed truncation semantics.
A stable frontend zero-witness guard plus whole-domain nonzero-divisor proof preserve dividend-signed remainder semantics.
A dual-valued Boolean literal retains typed intent until the backend legalizes it to a strict Verilog-2001 one-bit literal.
Opaque Boolean identities resolve only against distinct typed declarations and emit as explicit integer-equals-one predicates.
Negation preserves the shared default assignment and exact operand provenance while the emitter retains explicit grouping.
Conjunction retains both symbolic operands even when a default literal determines the witness, so unresolved references cannot hide behind short-circuiting.
Disjunction retains both symbolic operands and is rendered with deterministic Verilog precedence after complete reference validation.
